title: Machine Learning Engineer
tagline: Train, deploy and scale machine-learning models in production.
about: ML engineers take models from notebooks to production: building training pipelines, optimising models, serving predictions at scale and monitoring them as the world changes. The role sits between data science and software engineering, and needs real strength in both.
Expect more maths than most paths: linear algebra, probability and calculus underpin everything.
day: Train and tune deep-learning models in PyTorch
Monitor for data drift and retrain
Optimise models for cost and speed

phases.title: Programming foundations
phases.goal: Write small programs confidently and use the tools every developer uses daily.

nodes.d: Pick Python and get fluent with the basics before anything else. Fluency in one language transfers to every other.
links: CS50x: Harvard's intro to computer science

nodes.d: Developers live in the command line: navigating files, running programs and chaining tools together.
links: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education (MIT)
OverTheWire: Bandit (learn the shell by playing)

nodes.d: Version control is non-negotiable: every job uses it. Commit early, branch for experiments, open pull requests.
Break problems down, read errors calmly, use a debugger and print statements deliberately.
links: Exercism: practice in 70+ languages with mentoring

phases.title: Maths for ML
phases.goal: The three maths subjects ML stands on.

nodes.d: Vectors, matrices and the operations neural networks are made of.
Derivatives and the chain rule: how models learn.
Distributions, expectation, Bayes and the statistics of evaluation.
links: Seeing Theory: visual probability and statistics

nodes.d: Vectorised array programming: the language of numerical Python.

phases.title: Classical machine learning
phases.goal: Master the fundamentals with scikit-learn before deep learning.

nodes.d: Frame the problem, split data, choose metrics, avoid leakage.
links: An Introduction to Statistical Learning (free book)

nodes.d: Linear and logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting.
links: An Introduction to Statistical Learning (free book)

nodes.d: Turn raw data into signals models can use.
Accuracy is rarely enough: precision, recall, ROC-AUC, calibration.
Clustering and dimensionality reduction.

project.d: Pick a tabular dataset, build a leak-free pipeline, beat a strong baseline with gradient boosting, and write a clear report of what worked and why.

phases.title: Deep learning
phases.goal: Neural networks from scratch to transformers.

nodes.d: Build backpropagation by hand, then in PyTorch.
links: Andrej Karpathy: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero

nodes.d: Tensors, autograd, modules and training loops.
Convolutional networks and modern vision models.
links: Stanford CS231n: deep learning for vision
fast.ai: Practical Deep Learning for Coders

nodes.d: Attention, transformers and language modelling.
links: Andrej Karpathy: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero

nodes.d: Mixed precision, distributed training and experiment tracking.

project.t: Train a small language or vision model
project.d: Train a character-level GPT or an image classifier from scratch, track experiments, and publish a write-up with loss curves and ablations.

phases.title: MLOps & production
phases.goal: Models that run reliably in the real world.

nodes.d: Serve predictions behind APIs with batching and caching.
Reproducible data and training pipelines.
Track every run; promote models through stages.
Detect when the world changes under your model.
Package and scale training and serving.
Make models smaller and faster.

project.d: Deploy a model with CI-tested training, a registry, an API, monitoring for drift and an automated retrain path, all documented.

interview: ML fundamentals: bias/variance, regularisation, metrics, leakage.
Implement a training loop or a model component in PyTorch from scratch.
ML system design: recommendation, ranking, fraud detection.
Discuss a past project's trade-offs in depth.
certs: AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer – Associate (optional)
